feature_contract.goal: Prevent delayed +TIME/GOAL D3DXSprite batch use-after-free and stale source ownership across original game's sprite replacement, device loss and device reset.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Exact source-owned R64 game ID3DXSprite Draw/Flush/End/Lost/Reset and 0x55B218 live pointer, with no generic sprite flush, R84 stereo policy change, original input/FFB, SkyGlow, R26 rollback or frozen DXVK edit.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: C++ source showed BeforeQueueEnd could FlushTracked(TrackedSprite), dereferencing old sprite vtable with no live pointer proof. Meanwhile original LostDeviceDest and ResetDeviceDest used IsExactSprite(self) against global 0x55B218; a global cleared or replaced before callback skipped old owner invalidation. The combined stale ownership and vtable dereference is a concrete source-level crash/use-after-free path, with no HMD reproduction claim.
trace_stages: Original +TIME/GOAL GPU producers enter deferred ID3DXSprite Begin/Draw batches with StageExtensionTime/Goal semantic owner.
Game may clear or replace its 0x55B218 live pointer before old ID3DXSprite OnLostDevice/OnResetDevice callback, which previously missed tracked-batch invalidation.
QueueEnd or direct source exit must only Flush when candidate, tracked Begin owner and live 0x55B218 instance are identical; otherwise drop stale token before vtable access.
R84 physical dual-eye draw receives unchanged valid source and explicit unsafe fallback; final Windows game/host/package/Domain Gates remain required.
subcomponents: Capture callbacks against both retained old tracked identity and current live sprite before invoking lifecycle trampolines; invalidate exact pending source even if global changed.
Guard actual D3DX FlushTracked vtable dereference with three-way live instance identity; on replacement discard stale deferred ownership without issuing a GPU Flush.
Compile-time positive/negative source identity checks cover normal draw, silent replacement, null pointer, unrelated sprite and old tracked lifecycle callback.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Game-owned +TIME/GOAL deferred GPU batch and OnLostDevice/Reset callback
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Old object callback invalidates its previously tracked batch even when global pointer is null or replaced before native lifecycle invocation.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: QueueEnd and direct stage/goal GPU flush identity and native D3DX behavior
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Never dereference a stale tracked sprite vtable; only exact same candidate, tracked and live sprite Flush, otherwise fail closed to original game behavior.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: R84 Win32 DX9Ex Active, x64 host, R26_SAFE, package, Domain and source gate
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: All required GitHub Actions succeed on an identifiable exact validation-bearing SHA, separate from Quest3/VDXR untested hardware outcome.

source_trace: BeforeQueueEnd called FlushTracked(TrackedSprite) without a live game pointer equality check.
Lifecycle OnLostDevice/OnResetDevice tested IsExactSprite(self) against mutable game global 0x55B218 rather than retained Begin owner.
Identity guards now require candidate==tracked==live before vtable dereference and invalidate old owner from pre-trampoline callback evidence.
alternatives_rejected: Global Flush or cross-producer relabel would alter unrelated D3DX HUD/rank batching and has no demonstrated benefit; retain the exact strict original semantics.
diagnosis.original_evidence: Static C++ pointer lifetime defect, not user-confirmed headset reset crash.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: R84 dual-eye renderer/c64 transforms are unchanged; only invalid stale producer GPU batch submissions are vetoed.
diagnosis.hardware_causation: UNTESTED. Source-level invalid dereference path repaired; no Quest3/VDXR performance or optical result asserted.
